problem: The quadratic polynomial $P(t)$ has roots ${t}_{1}=4,{t}_{2}=3,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $2.$ Find $P(t).$

feedback.problem: The quadratic polynomial $P(t)$ has roots ${t}_{1}=4,{t}_{2}=2,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $-3.$ Find $P(t).$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since our quadratic polynomial has roots ${t}_{1}=4$ and ${t}_{2}=2,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=-3,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t-{t}_{1})(t-{t}_{2}) & =(-3)(t-4)(t-2) \\  & =(-3)(t-4)(t-2)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(-3)(t-4)(t-2) & =(-3)({t}^{2}-6t+8) \\  & =-3{t}^{2}+18t-24.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(t)=-3{t}^{2}+18t-24.$
